title: CI scope skips every job on a push that changes only docs/records.md when the head before the push was fully green
why: Owner ruling own-830-c-ci-scope-green-before-head (page item 830, option c, 15:02 CST Nov 14, no note); the owner chose a widening knowingly. Today a ready green PR meets a records-page push at merge (about 4 of 11 PR-merge commits since Nov 13 and 20 of 38 since Nov 10, triage's approximate count from a shallow clone) and a second full CI follows (44 min 32 s in the one run measured, n=1: run 43583006785, #3349 head 3128df369). The change, as the records lane described it (relayed, unread by triage): ci-scope.sh reads the push's before-head, checks that head's run was fully green and the push changed docs/records.md alone, then sets every job flag false; all-jobs-passed counts those skipped jobs as passed. It changes ci-scope.sh, checks.yml and lint/test_ci_scope.py, and edits the script's own fail-safe list, so it needs review round 3 and the net-value test. Unmeasured: the gain (jobs flagged false still start and skip), and a fail-safe against a wrong green read. GRANT SCOPE: only a push whose whole change is docs/records.md after a fully green head; any other change in the push runs CI as today. First act of a lane: read ci-scope.sh line 17 on (it diffs the whole PR against its base, never the push) and the test file, write the red tests first: a records-only push after a green head skips; a records-only push after a red or unknown head runs; a push that touches one other file runs; a hand-edited page does not skip beyond what main's check allows. Triage reads the before-head result as unknown when the run cannot be read, never as green. Kin: records-page-before-ready (the lane that described it), ready-push-merges-main (item 840), review-carries-own-record-commits.
